label: For the IB CS Internal Assessment (computational solution), first assessed May 2027 onward. Not for the Nov 2026 client-based IA.

sections.title: Problem specification
checklist: Say who the problem belongs to and why a computational solution suits it.
Describe the situation in your own words, with only the detail the reader needs.
Set out the requirements as success criteria you can later test (use the builder below).
Note limits on scope: what the solution will deliberately not do.

sections.title: Planning
checklist: Break the problem into smaller parts, and those parts into tasks.
Give each task rough start and end dates in the decomposition tool.
Link each planned task back to the success criterion it serves.
Show how the order of work was decided, and what you would do if a task slips.

sections.title: System overview
checklist: Show how the main parts fit together, using diagrams where a picture is clearer than words.
Mark the diagram positions with a [diagram: ...] placeholder so they are not counted as words.
Name the data the system stores and how it moves between parts.
Keep the overview short; detail belongs in the development section.

sections.title: Development
checklist: Pick the techniques that carry the solution and explain why each was chosen.
Point to the code excerpts in your register rather than pasting large blocks.
Show how you tested and fixed problems as you went, with evidence.
Make sure the full source code is in the appendix; the excerpts only highlight parts of it.
Credit any code or ideas you did not write yourself.

sections.title: Evaluation
checklist: Judge each success criterion honestly using the table below, with evidence for each.
Discuss how well the solution works: correctness, reliability and efficiency.
Say what feedback you gathered and what it changed.
Suggest specific improvements and extensions, and why they matter.

videoTips: Keep the whole video at five minutes or less.
Show the solution running against each success criterion, one shot per criterion.
Speak or caption what is happening; do not rely on the viewer guessing.
Rehearse once with a timer, then update the estimates below.
codeReminder: Reminder: the full source code must be included in the appendix for full marks in Development. This register only lists the excerpts you refer to.
